newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan to tell G7 fiscal reforms have priority--MOF.
newsitem.headline: Japan to tell G7 fiscal reforms have priority--MOF.

text.p: Japan will tell leaders of the Group of Seven (G7) nations at their summit meeting later this month that it will put priority on reforming government finances rather than expanding domestic demand, Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka was quoted as saying on Wednesday.

Mitsuzuka made the comment in a morning meeting with Shoichiro Toyoda, the head of Japan's Federation of Economic Organisations (Keidanren) and the chairman of a government panel studying state finances, a Keidanren spokeswoman said.

"I am aware that there are requests for expanding domestic demand, but I would like to put priority on restructuring state finances. We will be able to revitalise the economy through this," the spokeswoman quoted Mitsuzuka as saying.
She added that Mitsuzuka said he would like to explain this view to other G7 members when they meet in Denver for the annual G7 summit from June 20 to 22.
